extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians, computational algebraists, and programmers using Singular)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Singular commands and control-structure constructs: syntax, types/return values, purposes, notes/warnings and examples for correct use of functions like trace, transpose, uressolve, control statements (if/for/while), library loading, and package/identifier management.

rubrics_metrics.name: trace
rubrics_metrics.description: trace ( intmat expression ) / trace ( matrix expression ) — returns the trace of an intmat or matrix; type: int (for intmat) or poly (for matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: returns the trace. Example: intmat m[2][2]=1,2,3,4; trace(m); → 5. See related types intmat and matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: transpose
rubrics_metrics.description: transpose ( intmat expression ) / transpose ( matrix expression ) / transpose ( module expression ) — returns the transpose of the argument; return type matches argument (intmat, matrix, or module).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: transposes a matrix. Example shows transpose of 2x3 matrix producing 3x2. See intmat, matrix, module sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: type
rubrics_metrics.description: type name; or type ( name ); — prints the name, level, type and value of a variable (no return type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To display the value of an expression, evaluating the expression and ending with ; is sufficient. Example: int i=3; type(i); prints "// i int 3". See data types and related print/listvar/print functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: typeof
rubrics_metrics.description: typeof ( expression ) — returns the type of an expression as a string; if expression is an expression list, returns type of first list element; possible types enumerated ("ideal", "int", "matrix", etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: string. Note: internal only type is "?unknown type?". Examples show typeof(_) returning types after evaluation. See type command.

rubrics_metrics.name: univariate
rubrics_metrics.description: univariate ( poly expression ) — returns 0 if not univariate, -1 for a constant, or the number of the variable (index) if the polynomial is univariate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ring r=0,(x,y,z),dp; univariate(x2+1) → 1; univariate(x2+y+1) → 0; univariate(1) → -1. Can be used with var/univariate interplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: uressolve
rubrics_metrics.description: uressolve ( ideal expression, int expression, int expression, int expression ) — computes all complex roots of a zero-dimensional ideal using multipolynomial or sparse resultant algorithms and root-finding (Laguerre) steps; returns a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: second arg selects resultant algorithm (1 = multipolynomial, needs homogeneous ideals; 0 = sparse resultant); third arg sets fractional precision for Q ground field (otherwise ignored); fourth arg (0,1,2) gives number of extra Laguerre runs for improved results. Note: returned element types depend on ground field (number for complex ground field, otherwise string). See laguerre and mpresmat.

rubrics_metrics.name: vandermonde
rubrics_metrics.description: vandermonde ( ideal expression, ideal expression, int expression ) — computes the unique polynomial of degree d with prescribed values at given points (generalized multivariate Vandermonde interpolation); returns a poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/requirements: ground field must be Q; ncols(p)==n (number ring variables); generators must be numbers different from 0,1,-1; ncols(v)==(d+1)^n. Example provided for n=2, d=2 producing polynomial evaluated to given value. See Vandermonde system description and constraints in documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: var
rubrics_metrics.description: var ( int expression ) — returns the n-th ring variable (as poly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ring r=0,(x,y,z),dp; var(2) → y. See int, nvars, ring, rvar, univariate, varstr references.

rubrics_metrics.name: variables
rubrics_metrics.description: variables ( poly expression ) / variables ( ideal expression ) / variables ( matrix expression ) — returns an ideal listing all ring variables the argument depends on; return type: ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show variables(2) returning 0, variables(x+y^2) returning [x,y], variables(ideal(x+y2,x3y,z)) returning [x,y,z]. Can be converted to a string via string(variables(...)). See leadexp, nvars, univariate, var, varstr.

rubrics_metrics.name: varstr
rubrics_metrics.description: varstr ( ring name ) / varstr ( int expression ) / varstr ( ring name, int expression ) — returns string listing names of ring variables or the name of the n-th ring variable; returns type string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ring omitted, basering used. Examples: varstr(r) → "x,y,z"; varstr(r,1) → "x"; varstr(2) → "y". See charstr, nvars, ordstr, parstr, ring, var.

rubrics_metrics.name: vdim
rubrics_metrics.description: vdim ( ideal expression ) / vdim ( module expression ) — computes the vector space dimension of the ring/module modulo the ideal/module generated by initial terms of given generators; returns int, -1 if not zero-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If generators form a standard basis, equals vector space dimension modulo ideal/module. Example: vdim(std(i)) returns 4. See codim, degree, dim, ideal, kbase, mult, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: waitall
rubrics_metrics.description: waitall ( list expression ) or waitall ( list expression , int expression ) — waits for all links in list to be ready; returns int code (-1,0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expects list of open links (ssi:fork, ssi:tcp). Without timeout may block forever. With timeout (ms) forces termination. If timeout=0, polls without waiting. Return values: -1 = all links "eof" (maybe crashed); 0 = timeout/poll none ready; 1 = all links ready (note: some may be eof). Example demonstrates usage with forked processes and timeouts. See waitfirst.

rubrics_metrics.name: waitfirst
rubrics_metrics.description: waitfirst ( list expression ) or waitfirst ( list expression , int expression ) — waits until the first link in the list is ready; returns int code (-1,0, i>1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expects list of open links. Without timeout may block; with timeout behaves similarly to waitall. Return values: -1 = all links eof; 0 = timeout/poll none ready; i>1 index of first ready link. Example with multiple forked links and timeouts. See waitall.

rubrics_metrics.name: wedge
rubrics_metrics.description: wedge ( matrix expression, int expression ) — computes the n-th exterior power of matrix M; returns a matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: wedge(m,2) computes exterior power and prints components. See matrix, minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: weight
rubrics_metrics.description: weight ( ideal expression ) / weight ( module expression ) — computes an "optimal" weight vector for an ideal or module; returns intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: used as variable weight vector to speed up standard basis algorithm; if input is weighted homogeneous, finds a weight vector for which input is weighted homogeneous. Example computes intvec e for given ideal. See ideal, intvec, qhweight.

rubrics_metrics.name: weightKB (library standard.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: weightKB ( module expression, int expression , list expression ) / weightKB ( ideal expression, int expression, list expression ) — computes weighted degree-d part of a vector space basis (monomials) of quotient ring/module modulo I w.r.t. weights given by wim; returns same type as first argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: I,d,wim where wim is list of two intvecs (variable weights and module-generator weights). Generalization of kbase. Example: weightKB(ideal(0),3,intvec(1,2)) returns x^3 and xy. See kbase.

rubrics_metrics.name: write
rubrics_metrics.description: write ( link expression, expression list ) or for DBM links write ( link, string expression, string expression ) or write ( link, string expression ) — writes data to a link; return type none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: ASCII links convert expressions to strings separated by newline; ssi links write ring-dependent expressions with ring description; write blocks until ssi link ready for writing. To avoid evaluation before writing, use quote (and possibly eval). For DBM links: three-arg form inserts key/value; two-arg deletes entry. Examples: write ":w outfile", f,i overwrites file; write ":a outfile","that was f,i" appends; ssi format for large objects; read/execute example to restore saved objects. See dump, eval, link, print, printf, quote, read, short.

rubrics_metrics.name: block semantics (control-structure blocks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of commands surrounded by { and } defines a block used to group commands for procedures and control statements; blocks are required even for single commands and variables defined inside a block are not local to that block; ending semicolon at end of block is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variables defined inside block are not local; blocks used in procedures and to collect commands in if, else, for, while and library example parts. Example shows swap using a block. Important: block scoping differs from many languages—variables persist beyond block unless otherwise handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: apply
rubrics_metrics.description: apply( expression , function ); — applies function to all elements of first argument (which must be intvec, intmat, or list); returns an expression list whose type/format depends on following assign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function must be kernel command or procedure taking one argument and returning a value. Example: proc p(int x) {return(x^2);} apply(v,p) with v intvec returns list/vec of squares. Result formatting depends on assignment (intvec, list or expression list).

rubrics_metrics.name: break (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: break; — leaves the innermost for or while block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used inside loops to exit. Example shows break inside while/for. See for and while documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: breakpoint (debugging)
rubrics_metrics.description: breakpoint( proc name ); breakpoint( proc name, line no ); — sets a breakpoint at the beginning of the specified procedure or at the given line; line numbering rules described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: line number 1 is the first line of a library or the line with the { for procedures. A line number of -1 removes all breakpoints from that procedure. Example shows setting and removing breakpoints. See Source code debugger.

rubrics_metrics.name: continue (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: continue; — skips the rest of the innermost for or while loop and jumps to the beginning of the block; only valid inside for or while.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: unlike C, it does not execute the increment statement. Mainly for internal use. Example demonstrates altering loop variable then continue. See for/while.

rubrics_metrics.name: else (if/else)
rubrics_metrics.description: if ( boolean expression ) true block else false block — executes false block if boolean expression is false; only valid in combination with if.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if (i>5) { ... } else { ... } shown. See boolean expressions and if.

rubrics_metrics.name: export
rubrics_metrics.description: export name ; or export list of names ; — converts a local variable of a procedure to a global one (identifier is not removed at end of procedure) though package membership is unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Objects defined in a ring are not automatically exported when exporting the ring. Example shows exporting variables and an intmat. See exportto, importfrom, keepring.

rubrics_metrics.name: exportto
rubrics_metrics.description: exportto( package name , name ); exportto( package name , list of names ); — transfers an identifier in the current package into the specified package; the identifier is moved (no longer exists in current package).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: package name can be Current, Top or any package identifier. Warning: transfer removes identifier from current package; if copying desired use importfrom. Example shows exportto usage and resulting listvar outputs. Note ring objects are not automatically exported.

rubrics_metrics.name: for (loop)
rubrics_metrics.description: for ( init command; boolean expression; iterate commands) block — repetitive, conditional execution of a command block with init executed first, then boolean check, block execution, iterate commands, repeat until boolean false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: break leaves innermost for. Example: sum of 1 to 10 using for loop. See control structures, boolean expressions, break, continue, if, while.

rubrics_metrics.name: if (conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: if ( boolean expression ) true block or if ( boolean expression ) true block else false block — executes true block if condition true, else executes false block when present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses typeof to check matrix type before indexing. See boolean expressions, break, else.

rubrics_metrics.name: importfrom
rubrics_metrics.description: importfrom( package name , name ); importfrom( package name , list of names ); — creates a new identifier in the current package which is a copy of the one in package package name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Objects defined in a ring are not automatically imported when importing the ring. Warning: identifier is copied; original still exists in source package. Use exportto to transfer instead. Example shows importing pause from Inout and listvar changes. See export/import interactions and package management.

rubrics_metrics.name: keepring
rubrics_metrics.description: keepring name ; — (obsolete) moves the specified ring to the next (upper) level so a ring local to a procedure (and its objects) can be kept accessible after procedure ends without making ring global.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Command is obsolete; instead export identifiers from ring and return the ring. Can only be used inside procedures and should be last command before return. Example shows keepring usage and basering changes. See ring section.

rubrics_metrics.name: load
rubrics_metrics.description: load( string expression ); load( string expression , string expression ); — reads a library of procedures from a file; return type none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike LIB, load adds procedures to package corresponding to library, not to Top. Search path: current dir, SINGULARPATH, default dirs relative to executable, default absolute dirs. Second string selects options: "with" ≡ LIB, "try" ≡ LIB which never fails. Only procedure names loaded; bodies read at first call (lazy). Option to display loading messages (option(loadLib)). Examples of load, load(...,"try"), option(noloadLib) and listing packages via listvar(package). See libraries, dynamic modules, LIB command, package and proc sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: quit / exit
rubrics_metrics.description: quit; or exit; — quits Singular; works inside procedures or from an interrupt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synonymous commands; example simply shows quit;.

rubrics_metrics.name: return
rubrics_metrics.description: return ( expression list ); or return (); — returns the result(s) of a procedure and can only be used inside a procedure; brackets required even if no return value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: any. Can return multiple values (expression list). Example: proc tworeturn() { return (1,2); } and type-dependent returns (returning int or list) illustrated; callers may need def or list to collect values. See data types, proc.

rubrics_metrics.name: while (loop)
rubrics_metrics.description: while (boolean expression) block — repetitive conditional execution of block: evaluate boolean, if TRUE execute block and repeat until FALSE; break leaves innermost while.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates decrementing i and an infinite loop broken by break when a condition met. See boolean expressions and break.

rubrics_metrics.name: ~ (inline breakpoint / debug prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: ~; — sets an inline breakpoint: when Singular reaches ~; it prompts for input, allowing user to run Singular commands interactively; debug mode activated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User may input lines of Singular commands (line length ≤ 80); execution proceeds after an empty input line, continuing with command following ~;. Also activates source code debugger. Example shows ~; used inside procedure to inspect state before return.
